title: Jude and the Vow
premise: Odile Brightwater has built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly burying their own: eleven years ago, a letter confessing love was never sent, and the person it named—Jude Marlowe, now a rising political figure engaged to a dynasty's daughter—was left behind. When a misdelivered box of estate sale papers returns the unsent letter, Odile must decide whether to speak a decade-old truth before Jude's wedding, in three weeks, makes silence permanent. As Odile plans the very wedding that will erase their last chance, the two are pulled into late-night confessions, and Jude begins to question whether the life they've climbed into is theirs or a performance. In the end, at the rehearsal dinner, Odile finally says the rehearsed sentence aloud; Jude walks away from the altar not toward Odile, but toward themselves—and weeks later, on an ordinary Tuesday with no flowers or guest lists, they choose each other freely.
about_author: August Eastwick is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent six years behind the scenes of luxury weddings before trading seating charts for manuscripts. They write love stories about people who arrive late to their own lives and insist it still counts.

chapters.title: The Unsent
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. While cataloguing boxes from a client's estate sale, Odile finds their own eleven-year-old letter, postmarked but never delivered, returned undeliverable. The chapter establishes Odile's cynicism about weddings and their careful invisibility. Emotional beat: shock curdling into dread—the past has a return address now.

chapters.title: The Groom's Side of the Aisle
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile is hired to plan the wedding of Jude Marlowe and Vivienne Ashcombe, heir to a political dynasty, and realizes too late whose wedding it is. Jude doesn't flinch; Odile pretends not to either. Emotional beat: professional composure stretched over panic, first spark of old recognition neither can name.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Timing
chapters.summary: Alternating flashbacks woven through present-day venue walkthroughs. We see young Odile writing the letter, the misunderstanding that kept them apart, and Jude leaving town. Present-day Odile nearly burns the letter. Emotional beat: grief for a younger self who believed timing was everything.

chapters.title: Vivienne
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Sharp, generous, and exhausted, Vivienne reveals she knows she's a strategic match—and suspects Jude loves someone else. She hires Odile partly as a test. Emotional beat: unexpected sympathy; the antagonist becomes the story's most clear-eyed observer of power's machinery.

chapters.title: Rain Check
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A storm strands Jude and Odile together after a tasting gone wrong. Wine loosens the decade: near-confessions, laughter that feels like trespassing. Jude admits the engagement feels like a campaign platform. Emotional beat: dangerous warmth—the past pressing against the present like weather.

chapters.title: The Guest List
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Pressure mounts: the Ashcombe family tightens control, Odile's business partner warns them off, and a tabloid sniffs around Jude's 'mystery history.' Odile hides the letter deeper. Emotional beat: fear hardening into self-erasure—staying invisible as a survival skill that's become a cage.

chapters.title: What Power Buys
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At an Ashcombe fundraiser, Jude watches favors traded and truths edited, then catches Odile watching them across the room. A stolen conversation on a balcony ends with Jude asking, 'If I walked out, would you be there?' Emotional beat: temptation made concrete; duty revealed as a debt someone else keeps collecting.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Two days before the wedding, Vivienne privately releases Jude from the engagement—she won't marry a man performing devotion. But Jude, terrified of scandal and of wanting, tells Odile it's too late to matter. Odile pockets the letter, saying nothing. Emotional beat: the lowest point; courage failing exactly when the door opens.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Climax. Odile's POV at the rehearsal dinner. Watching Jude deliver a flawless toast full of words that belong to no one, Odile stands, abandons the script of a lifetime, and says the rehearsed sentence aloud in front of everyone. Silence, then Vivienne raising her glass. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into release—the decade ends in one spoken breath.

chapters.title: An Ordinary Tuesday
chapters.summary: Resolution, dual POV. Weeks later: no venue, no guest list, no dynasty. Jude has stepped back from the machine, Vivienne thrives untethered, and Odile plans one last wedding—a stranger's, gladly. On a rainy Tuesday, Jude shows up at Odile's door with coffee and no agenda. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; belonging chosen, not performed, and second chances finally arriving right on time.
